en: Theragāthā 3.11 Tikanipāta, Paṭhamavagga [The verse is as follows: "Having abandoned the three stains, having cut off the five lower fetters, having crossed over the four floods, I am one who has reached the further shore. [The commentary is as follows: At Sāvatthī, it is said, there was a certain monk. He had abandoned the three stains (*mala*): the stain of lust, the stain of hatred, and the stain of delusion. He had cut off the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiya-saṃyojana*): self-identity view, doubt, attachment to rules and observances, sensual desire, and ill will. He had crossed over the four floods (*ogha*): the flood of sensuality, the flood of existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance. Thus, he was one who had reached the further shore. Seeing him thus established in the fruit of Arhatship, the Blessed One, out of compassion for him, spoke this verse. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, a certain monk was dwelling in a forest grove near Sāvatthī. He was one who had abandoned the three stains, cut off the five lower fetters, and crossed over the four floods. Seeing him thus established in the fruit of Arhatship, the Blessed One, out of compassion for him, spoke this verse: "Having abandoned the three stains, having cut off the five lower fetters, having crossed over the four floods, I am one who has reached the further shore. Hearing this verse spoken by the Blessed One, that monk, with a mind of deep faith, attained the fruit of Stream-entry. From that time forth, he was known as "The Elder Who Reached the Further Shore" (*Pāragu Thera*). Thus ends "The Elder Who Reached the Further Shore," the eleventh [verse] in the Third Chapter of the *Theragāthā*. The first section of the *Tikanipāta* is concluded.
The Verses of the Elder Upāli:
One should associate with the virtuous,
those of pure livelihood who are untiring; having gone forth out of faith, one should dwell in the Dhamma.
A wise monk who has newly gone forth,
Having gone forth out of faith,
one who is skilled in what is proper and improper—
